sections.title: Old Bus
sections.passage: The old bus bounced over the rickety bridge. There was a clatter as the engine cover flew off, hit the railing and disappeared.

responses.prompt: Why did the engine cover fly off?
responses.response: because the car bounced over the rickety bridge

sections.title: Monarch Butterflies
sections.passage:
Monarch butterflies lay their eggs on the underside of the swan plant. There the eggs can grow, safe from the wind and sun. When they hatch, the tiny caterpillars eat their egg shells. Then they start to eat the leaves of the plant they are on.

They eat all the time and grow quickly. As they grow, they shed their skins many times because the skin does not stretch to fit the new body. When they have finished growing, the caterpillars make cocoons and hang upside down from a leaf or the stem of the plant.

While they are inside their cocoons many changes take place. As these things happen the cocoons change colour from light to dark green.

After about three weeks the butterfly is ready to hatch. At first, the new butterfly is weak and unable to move, but it slowly gains strength and is able to fly away.

responses.prompt: Why are butterfly eggs not found on the top side of leaves?
responses.response: so they can be safe from the sun

responses.prompt: What do the caterpillars eat first?
responses.response: they start to eat the plant they are on

responses.prompt: What would happen if they didn't shed their skins?
responses.response: because the skin dosent strech to fit the new body

responses.prompt: What colour is the cocoon to begin with?
When is the butterfly ready to fly away?

questionScores.rationale: Too vague — the specific clue of pushing a button and waiting for lights to change points to a pedestrian crossing, not just 'shops or walking somewhere'.
Correctly identifies feeding as the father's action.
Correctly identifies reading from the page-turning clue.
Correct causal reasoning despite a minor slip calling the bus a car.
Correctly infers it fell into the water.
Captures the core idea of waiting, despite misreading 'line' as a queue rather than a fishing line.
Correctly links the moving/jerking line to his excitement.
Correctly captures the safety rationale (from sun), matching the passage.
Incorrect — caterpillars eat their egg shells first, then move on to the leaves.
Restates the reason skins are shed rather than inferring the consequence of not shedding (e.g. the skin becoming too tight to grow).
Correctly identifies light green as the starting colour.
Correctly identifies gaining strength as the trigger to fly away.
